Indra. The king of the gods and the lord of storms, thunder, and rain in Hindu and Vedic tradition.

Indra commands the celestial army and rules over the heavens, governing all divine beings and celestial forces. As the god of storms, thunder, lightning, and rain, he wields the Indra danda, his thunderbolt or club, as his primary weapon. He rides upon Airavata, a white four-tusked elephant that serves as his divine mount.

Indra is depicted with multiple eyes, which symbolize his omniscience and his ability to perceive all events across the universe. He holds the vajra, the thunderbolt—the most powerful weapon in Hindu mythology. This weapon was forged from the bones of the celestial sage Dadhichi.

The Vedas celebrate Indra for his great victory over the demon Vritra, a serpent who hoarded water and prevented rain from falling. Through his martial prowess, Indra maintains cosmic order and is celebrated as a warrior deity of immense power. He is associated with courage, heroism, and martial virtues, making him a patron of warriors and rulers.

Though Indra is supreme among the gods, he remains subject to the cycles of cosmic time. In later Hindu mythologies, he can be challenged or even dethroned. Yet his role as king of the Devas and guardian of the heavens remains central to the Hindu understanding of divine hierarchy and cosmic maintenance.
